protocol_type: Controller-mastered command-driven parallel memory bus. Every command is decoded from the simultaneous state of CKE / CS# / RAS# / CAS# / WE# at a rising edge of CK; address / bank fields encode the operand. Data transfers are double-data-rate on DQ, framed by bidirectional differential DQS.

legend.RFU: Reserved for Future Use; must be programmed to 0
legend.V: H or L but a defined logic level

notes: 1. All DDR3 commands are defined by states of CS#, RAS#, CAS#, WE# and CKE at the rising edge of CK. The MSB of BA, RA, CA are device-density and configuration dependent.
2. RESET# is Low-enable; must be HIGH during normal operation.
3. Bank addresses (BA) determine which bank is operated upon. For (E)MRS, BA selects an (Extended) Mode Register.
4. V means H or L (but a defined logic level); X means either defined or undefined (floating).
5. Burst reads/writes cannot be terminated or interrupted; Fixed BL or BL-on-the-fly is determined by MR0.
6. Power-Down Mode does not perform any refresh function.
7. ODT does not affect the states; ODT not available during Self-Refresh.
9. VREF (VrefDQ and VrefCA) must be maintained during Self-Refresh.
10. NOP should be used when DDR3 SDRAM is idle or wait. NOP does not terminate an in-progress burst.
11. DES (Deselect) performs the same function as NOP.
12. Refer to CKE Truth Table for CKE transition detail.

channels.name: CK, CK#
channels.description: Differential clock; all command/address/CKE/ODT signals are sampled on the rising edge of CK (falling edge of CK#). All DDR3 internal timing is referenced to this clock.

channels.name: CKE
channels.description: Clock enable. HIGH activates internal clock and IO; LOW initiates Power-Down (active or precharge) or Self-Refresh. Asynchronous for Self-Refresh exit.

channels.name: CS#
channels.description: Chip select / rank select. HIGH masks all commands. CS#=L is part of every command code except DES.

channels.name: RAS#, CAS#, WE#
channels.description: Command inputs. Decoded with CS# to select MRS / REF / SRE / PRE / PREA / ACT / RD / WR / RDA / WRA / NOP / ZQCL / ZQCS.

channels.name: BA[2:0]
channels.description: Bank address. Selects 1 of 8 banks during ACT / RD / WR / PRE; selects mode register MR0..MR3 during MRS.

channels.name: A[15:0]
channels.description: Multiplexed row / column / op-code address. A10/AP doubles as auto-precharge during RD/WR; A10/AP doubles as one-bank-vs-all-banks during PRE; A12/BC# doubles as on-the-fly burst chop select during RD/WR.

channels.name: DM (DMU/DML for x16)
channels.description: Write data mask. When HIGH coincident with valid DQ on DQS edges, the corresponding write byte is masked (not written).

channels.name: ODT
channels.description: On-die termination control. Enables internal RTT termination on DQ/DQS/DM/TDQS in Synchronous / Dynamic / Asynchronous ODT modes. Honoured only when MR1/MR2 RTT bits are non-zero.

channels.name: RESET#
channels.description: Active-low asynchronous reset. Forces DRAM into reset state; must be HIGH during normal operation. CMOS rail-to-rail input.

channels.name: DQ[7:0] (x8)
channels.description: Data bus. Source-synchronous double-data-rate; sampled by receiver on both edges of DQS.

channels.name: DQS, DQS#
channels.description: Data strobe. Edge-aligned with DQ during read (driven by DRAM); centred in DQ during write (driven by controller).

channels.name: TDQS, TDQS#
channels.direction: SDRAM → controller (output, x8 only when MR1 A11=1)
channels.description: Termination Data Strobe; mirror of DQS termination for systems that need an additional termination output.

channels.name: ZQ
channels.description: Connected to ground via a 240 Ω ±1% external resistor; reference for ZQ calibration of output driver and ODT impedance.

channels.name: VREFDQ
channels.description: Reference voltage for DQ input thresholds (typically VDDQ/2).

channels.name: VREFCA
channels.description: Reference voltage for command/address input thresholds (typically VDD/2).

valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no per-beat handshake on the wire. Every command is committed at the rising edge of CK; data follows the command at deterministic latency.
READ data appears on DQ at Read Latency RL = AL + CL from the READ command; the SDRAM drives DQS edge-aligned with DQ.
WRITE data is launched by the controller at Write Latency WL = AL + CWL from the WRITE command; controller drives DQS centred in DQ.
tCCD (Column-to-Column Delay) shall be ≥ 4 nCK between successive READ/WRITE commands to the same rank.
tWTR (Write-to-Read delay) and tRTW timing rules govern direction turn-around on the bidirectional DQ/DQS bus.

frame_format.command_frame: One clock cycle on CK/CK#: CKE / CS# / RAS# / CAS# / WE# define command type; BA[2:0] + A[15:0] carry operands; sampled on rising CK.
frame_format.data_frame_BL8: 8-beat burst on DQ launched at fixed latency; clocked by DQS on both edges (4 CK cycles total).
frame_format.data_frame_BC4: 4-beat burst on DQ (chop); internally still consumes 4 CK cycles between successive commands (tCCD) — the controller cannot reuse the chopped half for another bank.
